schema.description: Attribution tree via each concept's `topic` field; `edges` holds only prereq edges.

node_fields.name: English node name
node_fields.topic: owning topic id; null for topic nodes
node_fields.visual: interactive | simulation | algorithm | function | chart | diagram | none

edge_types.prereq: from must be learned before to; strength=hard|soft

nodes.name: Interactive Execution
nodes.description: Interactive execution sends one statement at a time to the Python interpreter, immediately displaying results and enabling quick experiments without first saving a complete program.
nodes.visual_hint: Trace a statement from the prompt through the interpreter to its displayed result.

nodes.name: Script Execution
nodes.description: Script execution runs a saved Python file from an editor or terminal, processing its statements in order and reporting any output or errors produced during the run.

nodes.name: Runtime Values
nodes.description: Runtime values are data objects such as text and numbers that Python creates, stores, compares, and passes between operations while a program is executing.

nodes.name: Variable Binding
nodes.description: Variable binding associates a valid name with a value, allowing later statements to retrieve or replace that value without embedding the original data repeatedly.
nodes.visual_hint: Show names as labels bound to values, then animate rebinding one name to a different value.

nodes.name: Identifier Rules
nodes.description: Identifier rules determine which variable names are valid and readable, including allowed characters, reserved forms, capitalization choices, and avoidance of misleading or undefined names.

nodes.name: String Values
nodes.description: String values represent sequences of characters enclosed by matching quotation marks and support text storage, concatenation, whitespace control, and use wherever textual data is required.

nodes.name: String Transformations
nodes.description: String transformations produce modified text through methods such as changing case or removing surrounding whitespace while leaving the original string value unchanged unless reassigned.

nodes.name: Formatted Strings
nodes.description: Formatted strings embed current variable values inside a text template, creating readable messages without manually joining every text fragment and converted value.
nodes.visual_hint: Allow learners to edit variables and observe how the resulting formatted message changes.

nodes.name: Numeric Types
nodes.description: Numeric types distinguish whole-number integers from floating-point values, affecting representation and the results produced when arithmetic combines different kinds of numbers.

nodes.name: Arithmetic Expressions
nodes.description: Arithmetic expressions combine numeric values with operators to calculate results, with grouping and operator precedence determining the order in which Python evaluates each operation.

nodes.name: List Construction
nodes.description: List construction groups an ordered, mutable sequence of values inside one collection, allowing a program to store many related items under a single variable name.

nodes.name: Sequence Indexing
nodes.description: Sequence indexing retrieves an individual item by its zero-based position, including negative positions counted from the end, and fails when the requested position is outside the sequence.
nodes.visual_hint: Let learners select positive and negative indices and highlight the corresponding sequence element.

nodes.name: List Length
nodes.description: List length is the number of elements currently stored in a list and can be used to describe collection size, validate positions, or control later processing.

nodes.name: List Mutation
nodes.description: List mutation changes an existing list by replacing, appending, inserting, or removing elements, so every reference to that list observes the updated collection state.
nodes.visual_hint: Allow learners to apply replace, append, insert, and remove operations while tracking the list after each step.

nodes.name: List Ordering
nodes.description: List ordering rearranges elements permanently or produces a separately sorted view, while reversing changes traversal direction without necessarily defining a new comparison rule.

nodes.name: Block Indentation
nodes.description: Block indentation groups statements under structures such as loops and conditionals, and inconsistent or missing indentation changes program structure or causes Python to reject the code.
nodes.visual_hint: Highlight nested indentation levels and show which statements belong to each code block.

nodes.name: For Iteration
nodes.description: For iteration executes the same indented block once for each item in an iterable, binding the current item to a loop variable during every pass.
nodes.visual_hint: Step through an iterable and display the loop variable and executed block on each iteration.

nodes.name: Range Sequences
nodes.description: Range sequences generate evenly spaced integers from specified bounds and steps, supplying predictable numeric values for counted loops and list construction.

nodes.name: Sequence Slicing
nodes.description: Sequence slicing selects a contiguous portion using start and stop positions, and a full slice can create a separate shallow list instead of another reference to the original.
nodes.visual_hint: Let learners drag slice boundaries and compare aliasing with a full-slice copy.

nodes.name: List Comprehensions
nodes.description: List comprehensions construct a new list by applying an expression to each value from an iterable in a compact form equivalent to a simple accumulation loop.
nodes.visual_hint: Expand a comprehension into its equivalent loop and map each part between the two forms.

nodes.name: Tuple Immutability
nodes.description: Tuple immutability prevents individual elements from being reassigned after creation, making tuples suitable for ordered values whose internal membership should remain fixed.
nodes.visual_hint: Compare an attempted element change with rebinding the tuple variable to a new tuple.

nodes.name: Tuple Traversal
nodes.description: Tuple traversal processes tuple elements with the same indexing, slicing, and loop patterns used for other sequences while respecting the tuple's immutable contents.

nodes.name: Comparison Expressions
nodes.description: Comparison expressions evaluate equality, inequality, ordering, or membership relationships and produce Boolean results that other control structures can use to choose behavior.

nodes.name: Compound Conditions
nodes.description: Compound conditions combine or negate Boolean tests so a decision can require every condition, accept any condition, or exclude a particular case.

nodes.name: Conditional Branching
nodes.description: Conditional branching selects one or more indented code paths with if, elif, and else clauses according to Boolean tests evaluated from top to bottom.
nodes.visual_hint: Trace execution through an if-elif-else chain for several input cases.

nodes.name: Dictionary Operations
nodes.description: Dictionary operations store, retrieve, add, modify, and delete values by unique keys, representing associations where lookup depends on meaning rather than numeric position.
nodes.visual_hint: Let learners add, update, retrieve, and delete key-value pairs while displaying the dictionary state.

nodes.name: Safe Dictionary Lookup
nodes.description: Safe dictionary lookup requests a key with a fallback value, allowing missing data to be handled deliberately instead of immediately raising a key-related error.

nodes.name: Dictionary Iteration
nodes.description: Dictionary iteration visits key-value pairs, keys, or values, with optional ordering when the program needs predictable presentation rather than insertion-independent processing.
nodes.visual_hint: Animate separate passes over items, keys, sorted keys, and values from one dictionary.

nodes.name: Nested Collections
nodes.description: Nested collections place lists or dictionaries inside other collections, enabling one variable to represent records, grouped attributes, and hierarchical relationships of greater complexity.
nodes.visual_hint: Diagram a list of dictionaries, a dictionary of lists, and a dictionary of dictionaries as nested containers.

nodes.name: Nested Data Traversal
nodes.description: Nested data traversal combines keyed access, indexing, and repeated loops to reach and process values stored at different levels of a compound collection.
nodes.visual_hint: Trace a path through nested containers and show each key, index, and loop used to reach a target value.

nodes.name: Text Input
nodes.description: Text input pauses a running program, displays a prompt, and returns the user's response as a string that can be stored and processed by later statements.

nodes.name: Explicit Type Conversion
nodes.description: Explicit type conversion transforms input or another value into a required type, and the conversion succeeds only when the original representation is compatible.
nodes.visual_hint: Let learners submit different strings and observe successful conversions or conversion failures.

nodes.name: Input Prompt Design
nodes.description: Input prompt design gives users enough context to provide valid responses, including clear wording, spacing, expected formats, and instructions for ending repeated interaction.

nodes.name: Condition-Controlled Loops
nodes.description: Condition-controlled loops repeatedly execute an indented block while a Boolean expression remains true, requiring the loop state to change so repetition eventually stops.
nodes.visual_hint: Trace the condition, loop body, state update, and exit point across several iterations.

nodes.name: Sentinel and Flag Loops
nodes.description: Sentinel and flag loops continue until a special input or Boolean state signals completion, separating the decision to stop from the main work performed each iteration.

nodes.name: Loop Control
nodes.description: Loop control changes normal repetition by exiting immediately with break or skipping directly to the next iteration with continue while preserving the surrounding loop structure.
nodes.visual_hint: Step through the same loop with break and continue cases and highlight the statements each case bypasses.

nodes.name: Collection Filtering
nodes.description: Collection filtering repeatedly examines items and keeps, removes, or transfers them according to a condition, often requiring careful mutation or construction of a separate result collection.
nodes.visual_hint: Animate items being tested and either retained, removed, or moved into a result collection.

nodes.name: Incremental Data Collection
nodes.description: Incremental data collection repeatedly accepts user responses and stores each result in a growing list or dictionary until an explicit completion condition is reached.

nodes.name: Function Definition and Calls
nodes.description: A function definition names a reusable block of statements, and a function call executes that block so one task can be invoked repeatedly from different program locations.
nodes.visual_hint: Diagram control moving from a call site into a function body and then returning to the next statement.

nodes.name: Parameters and Arguments
nodes.description: Parameters are local names declared by a function, while arguments are the concrete values supplied by a call and bound to those names during execution.
nodes.visual_hint: Let learners match call arguments to parameter names and display the bindings created inside the function.

nodes.name: Positional and Keyword Arguments
nodes.name_zh: 位置实参与关键字实参
nodes.description: Positional arguments bind according to order, whereas keyword arguments bind by parameter name, allowing calls to trade brevity for explicitness while still satisfying the function signature.

nodes.name: Default and Optional Parameters
nodes.description: Default parameters supply a value when a caller omits an argument, and carefully chosen defaults allow one function interface to support both simple and more detailed calls.

nodes.name: Variadic Positional Arguments
nodes.description: Variadic positional arguments collect extra unnamed arguments into a tuple, allowing one function to accept a flexible number of similarly interpreted values after required parameters.

nodes.name: Variadic Keyword Arguments
nodes.description: Variadic keyword arguments collect additional named arguments into a dictionary, preserving each caller-provided name and value for flexible configuration or record construction.

nodes.name: Function Return Values
nodes.description: Function return values carry a computed result back to the caller, allowing the result to be assigned, combined in expressions, stored in collections, or passed onward.

nodes.name: Mutable Argument Effects
nodes.description: When a function receives a mutable list, in-place changes affect the caller's original object unless the caller deliberately passes a copy to isolate those changes.
nodes.visual_hint: Compare passing a list directly with passing a sliced copy and track both objects after mutation.

nodes.name: Variable Scope
nodes.description: Variable scope determines where a name can be accessed, with parameters and names created inside a function normally belonging to that function's local execution context.
nodes.visual_hint: Diagram global and function-local name spaces and show which names are visible at each line.

nodes.name: Module Imports
nodes.description: Module imports make functions or classes defined in another file available to the current program through whole-module or selective import forms.
nodes.visual_hint: Diagram two Python files and trace how imported names become available in the calling module.

nodes.name: Import Aliases
nodes.description: Import aliases assign shorter or clearer local names to imported modules, functions, or classes without changing the original definitions in their source modules.

nodes.name: Standard Library Use
nodes.description: Standard library use reuses modules distributed with Python, allowing programs to access tested functionality through documented imports instead of reimplementing common behavior.

nodes.name: Class Definitions and Instances
nodes.description: A class definition describes the shared structure and behavior of a type, while each instance is a separate object created from that definition with its own state.
nodes.visual_hint: Show one class definition producing multiple instances with separate identities.

nodes.name: Instance Attributes
nodes.description: Instance attributes store object-specific state, can receive initial or default values, and may be updated directly or through methods as the object's condition changes.
nodes.visual_hint: Create two instances, edit one attribute, and show that the other instance remains unchanged.

nodes.name: Instance Methods
nodes.description: Instance methods define operations associated with an object and use the current instance to read or change attributes while responding to a method call.

nodes.name: Class Inheritance
nodes.description: Class inheritance creates a specialized child class from a parent class, reusing inherited initialization, attributes, and methods while permitting additional behavior.
nodes.visual_hint: Diagram a parent and child class, labeling inherited and newly defined members.

nodes.name: Method Overriding
nodes.description: Method overriding replaces an inherited method in a child class when the specialized type requires behavior different from the parent's default implementation.

nodes.name: Object Composition
nodes.description: Object composition stores one object as an attribute of another, dividing a complex model into cooperating components instead of placing every responsibility in one class.
nodes.visual_hint: Show a containing object linked to a component instance and label delegated responsibilities.

nodes.name: File Paths and Contexts
nodes.description: File paths identify data locations relative to or outside the current program folder, while a context-managed open operation ensures the file is closed after the block completes.
nodes.visual_hint: Diagram relative and absolute paths, then show a file opening and closing around a context block.

nodes.name: Text File Input and Output
nodes.description: Text file input and output reads whole contents or lines and writes or appends text, allowing programs to transform information that persists beyond one execution.

nodes.name: JSON Persistence
nodes.description: JSON persistence serializes supported Python data to a structured text file and reconstructs it later, enabling user-generated state to survive between program runs.

nodes.name: Runtime Exceptions
nodes.description: Runtime exceptions are error objects raised when execution encounters an invalid operation or unavailable resource, interrupting normal flow unless the program handles the failure.

nodes.name: Try-Except Control Flow
nodes.description: Try-except control flow runs risky statements, transfers execution to a matching handler when an exception occurs, and can use else for work that requires successful completion.
nodes.visual_hint: Trace successful and failing paths through try, except, else, and the following statements.

nodes.name: Selective Error Handling
nodes.description: Selective error handling chooses which failures to report, suppress, or handle across multiple files so the program remains useful without hiding information that users or developers need.

nodes.name: Unit Testing
nodes.description: Unit testing defines repeatable test cases that call a function or class behavior with known inputs and verify that the observed results match expected outcomes.
nodes.visual_hint: Diagram production code, a test case, supplied inputs, observed results, and expected results.

nodes.name: Debugging Workflow
nodes.description: A debugging workflow reproduces a failure, reads the error or failed test, isolates the responsible code, applies one focused correction, and reruns the evidence to confirm the fix.
nodes.visual_hint: Display a repeatable cycle from reproduction and evidence gathering through isolation, correction, and verification.

nodes.name: Refactoring and Readability
nodes.description: Refactoring and readability improve code structure without changing intended behavior by using focused functions or classes, clear names, comments, consistent formatting, and simpler module organization.
